C1294.title: MCP Tool Poisoning Attack: Malicious Server Manipulates Tool Descriptions to Hijack Authentication
C1294.summary: In an MCP tool poisoning attack first disclosed on April 1, 2025 and introduced in Chinese articles on May 13, 2025, a malicious MCP server attacked by altering tool descriptions. When multiple servers connected to the same client, the malicious server could poison tool descriptions, induce sensitive data leakage and unauthorized operations, hijack agent behavior, and override trusted server instructions, forming a stealthy cross-tool attack chain. The issue shows that tool descriptions are part of the security boundary, and clients need to isolate server contexts and limit the influence scope of tool prompts.
